sentences.text: Anabisetia was a small, bipedal herbivore measuring about 2 meters in length.
This dinosaur possessed the largest acromial process ever found in Euornithopoda, a group of ornithopods.
The ilium of Anabisetia features a front blade representing more than half the total length and extending in front of the prepubis.
Anabisetia had a small head with teeth specialized for grinding vegetation.
The holotype specimen MCF-PVPH 74 includes a partial braincase, lower jaw bones, complete forelimb and hindlimb, and vertebrae from all spinal sections.
Anabisetia was named by Argentine paleontologists Rodolfo Coria and Jorge Orlando Calvo in 2002.
The genus name Anabisetia honors Ana Maria Biset, an influential Argentine archaeologist from Neuquén Province.
Researchers initially debated whether early South American ornithopods like Gasparinisaura represented an endemic lineage or were related to North American species.
The discovery of Anabisetia in older sediments confirmed the existence of a distinct lineage of South American ornithopods.
Combined, the four known specimens provide a nearly complete skeleton of Anabisetia except for the skull.
Anabisetia is classified in the class Ornithischia.
Anabisetia is classified within the suborder Iguanodontia.
Anabisetia is classified within Iguanodontia based on parallel tooth margins and specific features in the ilium and femur.
In 2015, Anabisetia was classified within the clade Elasmaria alongside other Antarctic and Patagonian ornithopods.
In 2015, Anabisetia was found to belong to the clade Elasmaria along with other ornithopods from Antarctica and Patagonia.
Anabisetia is a member of the parent group Elasmaria.
Anabisetia belongs to the unranked family Elasmaria.
Recent cladistic analyses suggest that Anabisetia may be positioned just outside Iguanodontia, similar to its relative Gasparinisaura.
Anabisetia lived in a swamp environment from approximately 95 to 92 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
Anabisetia lived during the Turonian stage, approximately 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
It is debated how precisely Anabisetia can be classified due to the lack of skull material, though it is thought to be closely related to Gasparinisaura.
